reason: Runnable and counted-structure metric (triple counts), has a null arm; but as written it cannot discriminate its own prediction. (1) Statistic/claim mismatch: claim is about max over ~p^2/2 models (2 log p bits of advice) but 20000 random (u,r) probe only the ~1e-4 tail; variance ratio >2 is not implied by a rare-model tail effect, and variance ratio 0.8-1.25 does not exclude it. (2) 'Poisson-like, KS p>0.01' is the wrong null: ordered triples are 6x multiply counted, sets are negation-closed (x-sets hold +/-P), |F| fluctuates (about half of x have points), so even random subsets are overdispersed vs Poisson; thresholds must be calibrated on the random-subset arm, not Poisson. (3) 'max/lambda grows with p' cannot separate p^eps from log p with two sizes (2^18, 2^20, factor 4); needs >=5 sizes with lambda and sample count held fixed. (4) Random (u,r) never samples the structured models (small step s=u^-2 mod p, small r, s=a/b small rationals) where any encoding effect would live; add deterministic structured arm. (5) 'k=8' undefined (summand count vs log2 B). (6) Toy says nothing about n=131 beyond the scaling exponent of max/lambda; even a positive log-factor is accounting by the idea's own admission, and 2 log p bits of advice cannot lower B*D^2 below N (brief rule 5), so no non-genericity certificate is reachable.
fix: REDESIGN. Setup: prime p, curve E with prime (or near-prime) order N, cyclic; build discrete-log table L[x] for both points +/-P above each x by walking multiples of a generator (about 1e6 affine adds at p~2^20, seconds; numpy/pure python, no Sage needed). Model (u,r): F_{u,r} = {x : u^2 x + r in [0,B)} = {s(t-r) : t in [0,B)}, s=u^-2; take points via L, set closed under negation. Metric = number of UNORDERED triples {a,b,c} in the log-set with a+b+c = R (mod N), summed over a fixed list of 8 targets R (reuse one sorted pair-sum array per model; pair-sums + searchsorted, ~O(B^2 log B) per model, B chosen so lambda per model is about 5 at each p, i.e. B~(30N)^(1/3) ~ 300 at N=2^20). Counted quantity, no wall time. ARM A (alg model orbit): 20000 random (u,r) per p. ARM B (control): 20000 random negation-closed subsets of x-values with the SAME |F| as the paired model (size-matched pairwise, both counted unordered). ARM C (structured): all s in {1..200} and s=a/b (a,b<=30), r in {0..B*4} plus r near p/2. ARM D (second control): same A-run on a different random curve and on a random bijection relabeling of F_p (kills any encoding effect by construction). Sizes: p in {2^14,2^16,2^18,2^20,2^22} (2^22 only if time). EXHAUSTIVE arm: at p<=2^12 enumerate the entire orbit (sliding-window over r per step s, O(p*(p/2)*B^2) with B~20, minutes) so the true max over all models is observed, not sampled. Statistics: (i) compare A vs B (not vs Poisson) by KS, variance ratio with bootstrap CI, and upper-tail exceedance counts at 99%,99.9%, and 99.99% quantiles of B (expected hits 200,20,2); (ii) fit tail slope of log P(count>=q) for A vs B; (iii) max_A/max_B and max/lambda versus log2 p across all sizes with lambda and sample count fixed: null predicts flat (or slow log growth, same in B), alternative predicts A above B with a rising gap; fit log(max/lambda) against log p vs log log p and report both. Pre-register: FALSE if variance ratio A/B in [0.9,1.1] with CI, KS p>0.01, tail exceedances within binomial 95% band, and ARM C max within null extreme-value band; TRUE-signal if ARM A or C exceeds the B 99.99% quantile by >3x binomial band at two or more sizes with a gap increasing in p. Budget: about 12-15 CPU-min at p up to 2^20 with numpy (A+B ~ 40000 models x ~10ms), exhaustive p<=2^12 about 3 min; drop 2^22. State in README that closure scope is 'interval bases under affine x-models, small toy sizes' and that no n=131 inference is made; if null, classify accounting and close model selection for interval bases only for this encoding family (x->u^2x+r), not for other non-uniform advice.
